evidence.claim: In 2022 Mexico recorded 696 attacks against the press, 12 journalists were murdered, 42.53% of documented attacks were perpetrated directly by state actors, and the executive branch made 176 stigmatizing comments against media, journalists, and civil society.
evidence.title: Mexico: Voices Against Indifference
evidence.excerpt: In 2022 Mexico recorded 696 attacks against the press, 12 journalists were murdered, 42.53% of documented attacks were perpetrated directly by state actors, and the executive branch made 176 stigmatizing comments against media, journalists, and civil society.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist annual report with quantified 2022 documentation and clear methodology.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: captures AMLO-era executive behavior and state-actor conduct in 2022.
contrary_evidence: Not every attack was personally ordered by the president.
Some violence was also driven by criminal actors rather than the federal executive.

evidence.claim: UN human-rights staff said leaked Sedena documents or a government-acquired software package revealed illicit surveillance against journalists and human-rights defenders, calling it grave, intimidating, and contrary to a safe environment for criticism.
evidence.title: La ONU-DH expresa su preocupación por actos de vigilancia ilícita contra personas defensoras de derechos humanos y periodistas
evidence.excerpt: UN human-rights staff said leaked Sedena documents or a government-acquired software package revealed illicit surveillance against journalists and human-rights defenders, calling it grave, intimidating, and contrary to a safe environment for criticism.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN country-office statement with explicit concern about government-linked surveillance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: it implicates federal authorities and the armed forces under AMLO.
contrary_evidence: The statement is not itself a court finding of personal presidential orders.
It addresses surveillance/intimidation more than kinetic violence.

evidence.claim: AMLO said the accusation that the reform sought his reelection was false and that the reform did not propose presidential reelection.
evidence.title: 16.11.22 Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said the accusation that the reform sought his reelection was false and that the reform did not propose presidential reelection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct ruler statement in an official transcript, but embedded in a partisan information campaign.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 statement about transfer rules and succession.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's own public position.
contrary_evidence: The same transcript also promotes a broad electoral overhaul that critics said would weaken independent institutions.
Self-denial is not independent proof of future compliance.

evidence.claim: R3D and Citizen Lab found that Mexican journalists and a human rights defender were infected with Pegasus between 2019 and 2021, after Mexico's president had assured the public the government no longer used the spyware and that there would be no further abuses.
evidence.title: New Pegasus Spyware Abuses Identified in Mexico
evidence.excerpt: R3D and Citizen Lab found that Mexican journalists and a human rights defender were infected with Pegasus between 2019 and 2021, after Mexico's president had assured the public the government no longer used the spyware and that there would be no further abuses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Technical forensic validation by a university lab, with explicit limits on attribution to a particular customer.
evidence.period_fit: Target-period relevant because the infections span into the AMLO years and were publicly reported in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The source places the infections during AMLO's government and after his public assurance, but does not identify the specific customer or direct order giver.
contrary_evidence: The lab explicitly says it could not attribute the hacking to a particular NSO customer.
The infections span 2019-2021, so the source is only partly target-year specific.

evidence.claim: AMLO's daily morning briefings became more aggressive toward journalists; in July 2021 he added a 'Who's Who' segment naming journalists and outlets he said published false stories, and he divides media into 'good' and 'bad' camps.
evidence.title: México
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
evidence.excerpt: AMLO's daily morning briefings became more aggressive toward journalists; in July 2021 he added a 'Who's Who' segment naming journalists and outlets he said published false stories, and he divides media into 'good' and 'bad' camps.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: University-based journalism research center; contemporaneous country report with clear description of AMLO's repeated public behavior.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 Mexico media environment during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's own public communication style; it does not by itself prove falsehood on any single story, but it does show his chosen rhetoric and targeting of critics.
contrary_evidence: Mexico still had active independent media and public criticism; the report is descriptive and does not adjudicate specific accusations.

evidence.claim: AMLO publicly revealed the alleged salary of Carlos Loret de Mola, a journalist who had reported on his family, and the article says many believed the details were illegally acquired from tax authorities.
evidence.title: Mexican president lashes out at EU 'lies' over his media-bashing rhetoric
evidence.excerpt: AMLO publicly revealed the alleged salary of Carlos Loret de Mola, a journalist who had reported on his family, and the article says many believed the details were illegally acquired from tax authorities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable international newspaper citing contemporaneous reporting and direct political reaction; the tax-leak implication is reported rather than independently proven in the article.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's response to criticism; the underlying salary data leak is not independently adjudicated here.
contrary_evidence: The article does not prove the tax-authority leak; it reports suspicion and criticism from observers.

evidence.claim: AMLO said the investigation into his son's alleged conflict of interest was open, asked who owned the Houston house and what Pemex contracts were involved, but also said investigators would find nothing and later attacked the reporter who broke the story.
evidence.title: López Obrador dice que está 'abierta la investigación' contra su hijo
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said the investigation into his son's alleged conflict of interest was open, asked who owned the Houston house and what Pemex contracts were involved, but also said investigators would find nothing and later attacked the reporter who broke the story.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Wire-based report with direct quotations from AMLO and the surrounding controversy; the underlying allegations remained unproven in the article.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's public response to allegations involving his son and a contractor-linked house.
contrary_evidence: The article does not establish wrongdoing; it records allegations, AMLO's denial, and a call for formal investigation.

evidence.claim: The European Parliament said Mexican authorities had shown systematic criticism and intimidation of journalists, cited clear signs of Pegasus use against journalists and rights defenders, and warned that AMLO-era electoral and judicial reforms raised rule-of-law concerns.
evidence.title: Mexico: The EP calls for the protection of journalists and activists to be guaranteed
evidence.excerpt: The European Parliament said Mexican authorities had shown systematic criticism and intimidation of journalists, cited clear signs of Pegasus use against journalists and rights defenders, and warned that AMLO-era electoral and judicial reforms raised rule-of-law concerns.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Formal parliamentary resolution by a major external institution, contemporaneous with the target year, with specific findings and concerns.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Targets the AMLO administration and its rhetoric/policies; it does not itself prove personal criminal intent, but it is directly relevant to ruler-level tolerance and use of power.
contrary_evidence: A parliamentary resolution is political monitoring, not a court judgment; it does not conclusively establish personal wrongdoing by AMLO.

evidence.claim: AMLO's government response to the European Parliament called its members 'borregos' and described the critics as part of a corrupt, reactionary, coup-minded group.
evidence.title: 11.03.22 Version estenografica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, desde Chiapas
evidence.excerpt: AMLO's government response to the European Parliament called its members 'borregos' and described the critics as part of a corrupt, reactionary, coup-minded group.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary transcript of AMLO's own words; self-serving, but direct evidence of his rhetoric toward critics.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's own public speech.
contrary_evidence: The statement is a political response and does not prove literal falsehood in the underlying EU criticism.

evidence.claim: AMLO said his electoral reform would guarantee clean and free elections, leave behind electoral fraud, and prevent any government, company, or economic power from buying votes.
evidence.title: Presidente presenta iniciativa de reforma electoral; incluye creacion del INEC y reduccion de gasto a partidos politicos
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said his electoral reform would guarantee clean and free elections, leave behind electoral fraud, and prevent any government, company, or economic power from buying votes.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraph and quoted reform justification
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official statement; useful for stated intent, but self-serving and not proof of effect.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's stated commitment, but the claim is about intent rather than verified effect.
contrary_evidence: Later reporting and opposition criticism argued the reform could weaken electoral independence.

evidence.claim: AMLO described the 'Who's Who in Lies' segment as a summary of media lies and social-media manipulation, and framed critical media coverage as false.
evidence.title: 07.09.22 Version estenografica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador
evidence.excerpt: AMLO described the 'Who's Who in Lies' segment as a summary of media lies and social-media manipulation, and framed critical media coverage as false.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary transcript of AMLO's own words and the official framing of the government segment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's own public communication strategy.
contrary_evidence: An official fact-checking segment can be legitimate in principle, but the phrasing here is overtly stigmatizing and not neutral.

evidence.claim: The SFP issued an 'Acuerdo de Conclusion por Falta de Elementos' and reported no evidence supporting conflict of interest, cohecho, or soborno involving AMLO, his son, and Daniel Chavez in the 'Casa Gris' matter.
evidence.title: La SFP exonera a AMLO, su hijo y Daniel Chavez de conflicto de interes
evidence.excerpt: The SFP issued an 'Acuerdo de Conclusion por Falta de Elementos' and reported no evidence supporting conflict of interest, cohecho, or soborno involving AMLO, his son, and Daniel Chavez in the 'Casa Gris' matter.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Credible Mexican business-political reporting on an official administrative finding; the underlying finding is relevant but limited by jurisdiction and evidentiary scope.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly attributable to AMLO because the case touched his family and his administration's conflict-of-interest review; the finding is about absence of evidence, not proof of innocence.
contrary_evidence: The article itself notes criticism that the SFP lacked evidence and that its jurisdiction did not cover foreign transactions or acts outside the federal administration.

evidence.claim: The article says AMLO was seeking a Banxico successor more aligned with his political vision and that government job offers were being used as pressure as Gerardo Esquivel's term neared expiry.
evidence.title: Gerardo Esquivel rechaza ofertas laborales del Gobierno de Mexico
evidence.excerpt: The article says AMLO was seeking a Banxico successor more aligned with his political vision and that government job offers were being used as pressure as Gerardo Esquivel's term neared expiry.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Financial-news reporting based on unnamed sources; plausible and specific, but not fully documentary.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to AMLO's personnel preferences and the government's approach to Banxico appointments, though the sourcing is indirect.
contrary_evidence: Esquivel had earlier been an AMLO adviser and the article does not prove self-dealing or corruption; it is about alignment and institutional independence.

evidence.claim: AMLO withdrew his previous Banxico nominee and selected Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, a public-finance official with strong budget experience but little monetary-policy experience, prompting concerns about politicization of the central bank.
evidence.title: Factbox-Victoria Rodriguez, Mexico's new pick for central bank governor
evidence.excerpt: AMLO withdrew his previous Banxico nominee and selected Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, a public-finance official with strong budget experience but little monetary-policy experience, prompting concerns about politicization of the central bank.
evidence.source_locator: factbox bullet list and opening paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters factbox based on contemporaneous reporting and biographical detail; the loyalty concern is inferential but clearly stated by the article.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2021 nomination with a 2022 start date and 2022 consequences.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's nomination choice; the competence-versus-loyalty inference is based on the article's framing and market reaction.
contrary_evidence: The same article notes Rodriguez had extensive public-finance experience and formal economics training.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 evidence on AMLO's personal control over civilian-nuclear safety appointments, regulatory discipline, or command-side decisions is thin.
There is no Mexico-originating war, proxy conflict, or coercive peace leverage in 2022, so the dossier is mostly diplomatic posture rather than operational conflict conduct.
Specific chain-of-command evidence for some police, military, and intelligence abuses remains incomplete, especially for local versus federal responsibility.
Some of the evidence about electoral reform and media pressure is rhetorical or journalistic rather than a direct legal finding of intent to entrench power.
The causal split between AMLO policy, inherited weakness, and global shocks is still only partially recoverable for 2022 poverty, inflation, and investment outcomes.
Independent post-launch quality and outcome audits for IMSS-Bienestar, education recovery, and related welfare programs are thinner than the rollout record.
Direct documentary evidence of personal enrichment, hidden financial benefit, or knowing approval of surveillance remains limited.
Durability and post-launch independent audits for AIFA, Dos Bocas, IMSS-Bienestar, and the education programs are thinner than the implementation record.
